title: Food and Daily Life
subtitle: Cattle, grain, and the rhythm of the day
body: Cattle hold a central place in Murle daily life, providing milk, social status, and a measure of wealth used in important exchanges such as marriage. Herding responsibilities are often shared among family members from a young age.

Alongside cattle, sorghum and other grains form a dietary staple, cultivated during the rainy season and stored carefully to last through drier months. Meals are typically shared, reinforcing the community's strong sense of collective life.
The daily rhythm — waking with the herds, tending to crops, and gathering in the evening — has shaped social customs, storytelling traditions, and the timing of community events for generations.
As with other sections, more detail and firsthand accounts will be added here over time.
